messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Consuming UV-exposed mushrooms did not improve depression outcomes compared with control; no between-group differences in brain health indices.
Sentence: "Consuming UV light-exposed mushrooms did not improve brain health outcomes."
Measured as: depression (BDI-II, PHQ-9)
Population: Adults without severe depression, cardiovascular disease, or Type 2 Diabetes, age 43 ± 11 y, BMI 29.8 kg/m2
Intervention: Two daily servings (168 g/d) of UV-exposed cremini mushrooms providing ~800 IU/d vitamin D2 for 6 weeks
Comparator: 2 tsp/d breadcrumbs (control)
Design: non-randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 41
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Serum vitamin D was inversely correlated with depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 and HAMD-17) among depressed patients.
Sentence: "Spearman's correlation analysis revealed significant inverse correlations of vitamin D and triglyceride (TG) with PHQ-9 and HAMD-17 scores among depressed patients."
Measured as: depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 and HAMD-17 scores)
Population: 412 first-episode, drug-naïve patients with depression
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower serum vitamin D levels
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 592
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"A 6-week non-randomized mushroom-supplementation trial in adults without severe depression finds no effect, while a case-control study of drug-naive depressed patients finds an inverse serum vitamin D–symptom correlation; population and design differ most.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator"],"detail":"observational serum-level correlation in 412 depressed patients vs a 6-week non-randomized supplementation trial (n = 41) in adults without severe depression"}
